summary: At step 380, timeout.c:hatch_egg fires for a viable carried giant ant egg. JavaScript has no HATCH_EGG timer callback. The whole callback task must also establish its consumed makemon/tamedog source closure; existing implementations and old creation-route fixes do not supply whole-function completion evidence.

source.branch: A due TIMER_OBJECT uses the HATCH_EGG function index for a fertile carried egg on the current level. hatch_egg() derives ownership from egg->spe or the male-carrier rn2(2) branch, treats timeout == svm.moves as a visible hatch, rolls rnd(egg->quan), and creates a non-unique, non-genocided species with enexto() and makemon(). A successful own same-level hatch is tamed; the inventory branch reports the hatch, learns the egg species when visible, and consumes the egg or schedules a short timer for any remainder.
callers: C: timeout.c:1985 registers hatch_egg in timeout_funcs[HATCH_EGG]; timeout.c:2222-2242 run_timers() unlinks a due timer, decrements TIMER_OBJECT.timed, then calls the registered function.
C elapsed-turn path: timeout.c:947 nh_timeout() calls run_timers(); the assigned recording reaches this path at step 380.
C other production callers: do.c:1823 goto_level() and restore.c:930 restgamestate() also call run_timers().

Current JS elapsed-turn path: allmain.js:1310 preflights an entering turn through timeout.js:650 preflight_nh_timeout_elapsed_turn(); timeout.js:453 unportedDueTimerReason() stops because the HATCH_EGG row has no callback. The live timeout path is timeout.js:1211 nh_timeout() -> run_timers().
Current JS level-arrival path: do.js:2632-2635 calls timeout.js run_timers() after object and monster delivery.
dependencies: Whole-function scope is timeout.c:hatch_egg; update timeout.js timeout_funcs[HATCH_EGG] and due-prefix admission so this row has a callback while other unported rows still refuse safely. The current HATCH_EGG table row at timeout.js:376 has only a name, and unportedDueTimerReason() at :453 rejects every due row without f.

Result-bearing get_obj_location, enexto, makemon and tamedog determine location, spawn success and ownership. The accepted A83 get_obj_location and enexto/enexto_core/collect_coords/goodpos evidence is reusable: their JS files are unchanged since checkedAt 62092f3c6a618f508c18f57463366227f24d3f87. Whole makemon and tamedog evidence is absent from current function/required-function records and accepted whole-function spans; include their unowned source closure rather than treating old declaration flags or route-specific creation fixes as completion. Whole tamedog consumes dogfood and dog_eat, and dog_eat consumes dog_nutrition and dogfood, even though this egg caller passes obj=NULL and does not execute the food arms.

timeout.js already implements attach_egg_hatch_timeout() at :1710 and learn_egg_type() at :1728. Reuse these for remaining egg stacks and inventory knowledge; preserve the callback’s container_weight(), useup(), obj_extract_self(), obfree(), and newsym() effects through their existing JS owners.

C restore.c:930 is a third run_timers() caller; the current JS search found direct calls through nh_timeout() and goto_level() only. This case establishes the elapsed-turn route, so keep restore-path coverage separate from the cause of this mismatch.

evidence: The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20261003003219-v20.json identifies this case at evaluationCommit b5bb23ff11504c300f032b10b1e17c99b06fc97e, with 380/502 screens matched, 8541/11010 RNG calls matched, and a stop at step 380: “elapsed-turn nh_timeout requires a ported timeout function, but hatch_egg() is due”. The queue row carries remainingScreens=122 and the same evaluation commit.

The admitted recording challenges/cases/v20/hatch-viable-giant-ant-egg-protection-pager-corrected-v20.session.json records step 380 calls rn2(2)=0 and rnd(1)=1 at timeout.c:hatch_egg(), followed by hatch placement and makemon draws. At step 381 its screen reports “You see a giant ant drop out of your pack!”. This agrees with the callback branch in upstream timeout.c:1017-1187.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/timeout.c:1017-1187 defines the whole impure hatch_egg() callback, including egg viability, ownership and silent checks, location and hatch-count checks, monster placement and taming, inventory/floor/minvent output, egg knowledge, rescheduling or cleanup, and redraw. timeout.c:1976-1990 maps HATCH_EGG to the callback table; timeout.c:2222-2242 dispatches due timers.

At the examined JavaScript source, js/timeout.js:376 has no f for HATCH_EGG. js/timeout.js:453 refuses a due timer without f, and js/timeout.js:650 invokes that refusal during elapsed-turn preflight. js/timeout.js:1535-1545 applies the same due-prefix check before mutating the timer queue. The C source and saved evaluation therefore identify the same source owner and an actionable whole-function port.
